title: Why Jesus Called Some People “Blind”
paragraphs: You think Jesus was being harsh.

Calling people “blind”…
Religious leaders… teachers… the experts.
Because what He saw… wasn’t what they saw.
And this is where it gets uncomfortable—because the same condition still exists today.
There’s a moment where Jesus Christ looks directly at the Pharisees and says:
“They are blind guides. If the blind lead the blind, both will fall into a pit.” (Matthew 15:14)
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
They could quote it. Teach it. Debate it.

Spiritual blindness isn’t ignorance.
It’s seeing truth… and rejecting it anyway.
It’s knowing the words of God—but missing the heart of God.

Dust in the air. Sand underfoot.
Crowds pressing in.
And right in front of them stands the Messiah they’ve been waiting for…
Not because the evidence wasn’t there.
But because their pride was louder than the truth.
And if this is hitting deeper than expected… it’s not by accident.

• You can see miracles—and still doubt
• You can hear truth—and still resist
• You can follow religion—and still miss salvation
“For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind will see and those who see will become blind.”

Those who admit they’re blind… receive sight.
Those who claim they see… reject the Light.
And here’s the part many avoid:

It distorts truth.
It hardens the heart.
It convinces you you're fine… when you're not.
But this is where everything shifts.
Because Jesus didn’t just point out blindness—

You are spiritually blind because of sin.
You cannot fix it yourself.
But Jesus—fully God, fully man—came, lived without sin, died in your place, and rose again…
So that through repentance and faith…

From darkness… to light.
From pride… to surrender.
From blindness… to sight.
But here’s the question most people avoid:
What if the blindness Jesus warned about… is closer than you think?
And it’s expanding almost every day.
If this opened your eyes even a little—
And maybe that’s exactly why this found you.
